title: Pare Mountain Vegetable Stew
localName: Mchuzi wa Mboga za Milima — Wapare
community: Pare people of the Pare Mountains — the mountain farmers of northeastern Tanzania
author: Mama Salima

heritage.origin: Pare people of the North and South Pare Mountains, Kilimanjaro region
heritage.history: The Pare (Wapare) people inhabit the Pare Mountains — a range of dramatic, green peaks rising from the dry plains between Kilimanjaro and the coast. Their mountain environment is fertile and well-watered, producing a variety of vegetables, root crops, and legumes. The Pare are known for their sophisticated pre-colonial irrigation systems, which allowed them to farm the mountain slopes intensively. Pare mountain vegetable stew uses the diversity of produce from their terraced mountain gardens.

desc: Pare Mountain Vegetable Stew — a mixture of mountain vegetables including yams, pumpkin, green beans, and local greens simmered together in a simple broth with groundnuts. The vegetable wisdom of the Pare Mountains — using the diversity of what grows at altitude.
longDesc: Pare mountain stew is the most vegetable-diverse traditional stew in Tanzania — the Pare Mountains support a remarkable range of vegetables at different altitudes, and Pare cooks combine them in one pot with groundnuts for protein. It is vegetarian by practice rather than by philosophy — the mountains simply provide.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed mountain greens — spinach or amaranth
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden. Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Add yam and pumpkin. Stir to coat. Add water.
Cover and cook 12 minutes until nearly tender.
Add green beans. Cook 5 more minutes.
Mix groundnut paste with ½ cup warm water. Add to pot.
Add greens on top. Cover 3 minutes until wilted.
chefTips: Add harder vegetables first, softer last.
The groundnut paste enriches without dominating — do not over-add.
commonMistakes: Adding all vegetables at once — uneven cooking.
cookingScience: See TZA103 for mixed vegetable stew science.
sustainabilityTips: Pare mountain terraced farming is one of Tanzania's most sustainable agricultural traditions.
culturalNote: Pare mountain vegetable stew is the edible map of the Pare Mountains — each vegetable in the pot comes from a different altitude on the terraced slopes. It is the cuisine of careful stewardship and agricultural intelligence.
